Does knowing the referee improve the forecast?

Same matches, same algorithm, same pre-match context (market, both teams' discipline, league level, fixture context). The only difference is the referee features. Lift = context-only loss minus context+referee loss (log loss; Poisson deviance for card counts; squared error for card difference and stoppage time), ×1000. Bars: real referee lift with 95% interval (weekly block bootstrap). Orange dot: the same model fed placebo referees shuffled within league-season; real information must clear it.

Detail

Do referees genuinely differ?

Every trait is a residual against a pre-match expectation, so referees are not credited for the games they are given. Real share: part of the between-referee spread that is not sampling noise. Reliability: correlation between a referee's alternate matches (Spearman–Brown corrected); below ~0.2 a "profile" is mostly noise. p: permutation test, referees shuffled within league-season. P10–P90: spread of shrunk referee estimates. Whole sample, descriptive only: the forecasting models never see this table.

Home bias, pressure and game management: league-wide effects

Average residual over all matches with a 95% interval from a bootstrap over referees. Home-bias rows show how much decisions lean towards the home side beyond what the two teams' own histories predict. Slopes measure pressure: how far the decision index moves per unit of crowd size, favourite strength or a team's record of winning decisions. A population effect says officials as a group respond; the reliability column above says whether some referees respond more than others.
